title: A locally finite type pseudo torsor under an unramified group is unramified
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $B$ an algebraic space over $S$, and $G$ and $X$ algebraic spaces over $B$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Suppose $G$ is a group algebraic space: multiplication $m:G\times_B G\to G$, identity $e:B\to G$, and inversion $i:G\to G$ induce group structures on $G(T)$, natural in every scheme $T\to B$. Suppose $a:G\times_B X\to X$ is an action, so $a(gh,x)=a(g,a(h,x))$ and $a(e,x)=x$ on all test schemes. Assume that the morphism
$$G\times_B X\longrightarrow X\times_B X,\qquad (g,x)\longmapsto(a(g,x),x)$$
is an isomorphism; this condition defines a pseudo $G$-torsor and does not require $X\to B$ to be surjective. If $G\to B$ and $X\to B$ are locally of finite type and $G\to B$ is unramified, then $X\to B$ is unramified. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Local finite type and unramifiedness for algebraic spaces mean the corresponding scheme properties [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-unramified-morphism] on etale scheme charts of source and target.

source.place: Tag 0DSK (lemma-pseudo-torsor-implications), part (1); pseudo torsor is Definition 04TW (definition-pseudo-torsor).

proof.text: Write $f:X\to B$. For an arbitrary $z\in|X|$, choose a representative $x:\operatorname{Spec}K\to X$ using the field-valued description of points in [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Put $b=fx$, $X_K=X\times_B\operatorname{Spec}K$, $G_K=G\times_B\operatorname{Spec}K$ and $p:X_K\to X$. The same node supplies these algebraic spaces and their sheaf fibre products. The pair $(x,\mathrm{id})$ gives a section $s:\operatorname{Spec}K\to X_K$, whose image projects to $z$. Base changing the given pseudo-torsor isomorphism gives $\phi_K:G_K\times_K X_K\xrightarrow{\sim}X_K\times_K X_K$, with $\phi_K(g,t)=(a_K(g,t),t)$. This last assertion follows by taking the fibre product of the original isomorphism and its inverse.

source.place: Tags 0DSK(1), 04TW; reduction to a field with a point, using the given representative of z.

proof.text: The section $s$ gives an isomorphism $\theta:G_K\to X_K$, $g\mapsto a_K(g,s)$. Explicitly its inverse is $r(t)=\operatorname{pr}_1\phi_K^{-1}(t,s)$. Since the second component of $\phi_K$ is its second input, $\phi_K^{-1}(t,s)=(r(t),s)$, so $\theta r(t)=t$. Conversely $\phi_K(g,s)=(\theta(g),s)$ gives $r\theta(g)=g$. These formulas are morphisms of sheaves over $\operatorname{Spec}K$, so are mutually inverse morphisms of algebraic spaces.

source.place: Tag 04TX (lemma-characterize-trivial-pseudo-torsors), part (2); explicit verification of the omitted proof.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-space-unramified-permanence], $G_K\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is unramified, as a base change of $G\to B$. Hence $f_K:X_K\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is unramified: via $\theta$ from step 2 its source etale charts and their scheme structure morphisms are the very same charts as for $G_K\to\operatorname{Spec}K$. Thus the chart definition of unramifiedness is unchanged.

Apply [lem-sfb-space-unramified-locus-base-change] to the locally finite type morphism $f$ and the base change $b:\operatorname{Spec}K\to B$. It gives $U(f_K)=X_K\times_X U(f)$. Step 3 gives $U(f_K)=X_K$, so the point represented by $s$ belongs to $p^{-1}U(f)$ and consequently $z\in U(f)$. Since $z$ was arbitrary, the open subspace $U(f)$ is all of $X$, and $f$ is unramified. If $|X|$ is empty the same equality of opens is vacuous. No section over $B$, nonempty fibre over every point of $B$, flatness or finite presentation was assumed.

The item matches Stacks 0DSK(1) and 04TW (spaces-groupoids.tex l.603-720) hypothesis by hypothesis: pseudo-torsor isomorphism, G and X locally of finite type, G unramified, no surjectivity assumed. The statement and stmt_deps are unchanged and there are no new nodes. Live and side-live both still show the item unsplit, so it is not superseded. Step 1: lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers gives fibre products and field-valued points; the section is s=(x,id) and phi_K is the base change of the isomorphism and its inverse. Step 2: theta(g)=a_K(g,s) and r(t)=pr1 phi_K^{-1}(t,s); both composites checked on T-points, so the step is genuinely elementary (explicit 04TX(2)). Step 3: the base-change clause of lem-sfb-space-unramified-permanence makes G_K->Spec K unramified, and transporting this along the isomorphism theta over Spec K is elementary. Step 4: lem-sfb-space-unramified-locus-base-change applied to f (lft) and b gives X_K = X_K x_X U(f), so z is in U(f); an open subspace containing every point is X, a one-line consequence of the definitions. Edge cases checked: X empty, an empty fibre over a point of B, G=B (X->B a monomorphism), transcendental or inseparable K. Duplicate search found only lem-sfb-space-infinitesimal-lift-pseudotorsor and lem-sfb-group-space-unramified-identity-test, both different statements.
